title: Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble
subtitle: Nintendo · Game Boy Color

body: Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble is Nintendo's Game Boy Color action-puzzle game about rolling Kirby through stages by tilting the handheld itself. Sensors inside its distinctive pink cartridge read the movement and translate it into the character's direction. Dream Land has lost its stars, giving Kirby a reason to pursue King Dedede through the obstacle courses. The player looks down on a ball-like hero whose movement depends on the angle of the screen being held, joining the physical object and the world displayed inside it in one unusually direct action.

Tilting controls the roll, while a quick movement of the machine can pop Kirby into the air. The player balances momentum, direction and the timing needed to cross hazards before the stage's timer expires. Clock tiles and collected clocks provide extra time, making the route a choice between the destination and useful detours. The controls ask for awareness of the hands as well as the screen. A movement intended to correct the next turn also changes the angle from which the player is watching it happen.

Red stars hidden through the stages open more demanding versions of the worlds, encouraging a return once the unusual controls become comfortable. Nintendo released the cartridge in Japan in 2000 and North America in 2001. Kirby's round shape makes the hardware's purpose easy to understand: an apparently soft ball rolls in the direction the player tips the machine. The design turns an unfamiliar input into a recognisable toy-like action, then develops a complete obstacle course around learning to perform that action accurately.
